# camunda_cluster_encryption (Resource)

Manage the customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK) of a cluster on Camunda SaaS. The cluster must have been created with `encryption = "External"`, which requires the Enterprise plan and an AWS region. Creating the resource sets the keys and waits until the encryption is ready; changing the keys rotates them. The Console can't remove the keys, so destroying the resource only removes it from state and leaves the keys configured.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "camunda_channel" "this" {
  name = "Stable"
}

data "camunda_cluster_plan_type" "this" {
  name = "Production"
}

data "camunda_region" "this" {
  name = "Frankfurt, Europe (eu-central-1)"
}

resource "camunda_cluster" "byok" {
  name = "byok"

  channel    = data.camunda_channel.this.id
  generation = data.camunda_channel.this.default_generation_id
  region     = data.camunda_region.this.id
  plan_type  = data.camunda_cluster_plan_type.this.id

  # Required for customer-managed keys.
  encryption = "External"
}

resource "camunda_cluster_encryption" "test" {
  cluster_id     = camunda_cluster.byok.id
  primary_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:123456789012:key/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster ID
- `primary_key_id` (String) ARN of the AWS KMS key in the cluster's primary region. Single-region and multi-region (`mrk-...`) keys are accepted, as long as the region in the ARN matches the cluster's.

### Optional

- `secondary_key_id` (String) ARN of the AWS KMS key in the cluster's backup region. Required for dual-region clusters, must be omitted for single-region clusters, and must differ from `primary_key_id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID, which is the cluster ID
- `primary_key_arn` (String) ARN of the primary key, as the Console reports it.
- `secondary_key_arn` (String) ARN of the secondary key, as the Console reports it. Null if there is none.
- `status` (String) State of the encryption, `Ready` once the keys are in use.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Cluster encryption is imported by the cluster ID.
terraform import camunda_cluster_encryption.test '<cluster_id>'
```
